headline: Paraguay’s New President Overhauls Cabinet After Peña Ouster
content: (Bloomberg) -- Paraguay’s Pedro Alliana moved to put his stamp on the cabinet he inherited from his impeached predecessor, Santiago Peña, naming new ministers and asking senior officials from the previous administration to tender their resignations.Alliana swore in new interior and public works ministers and named a legal adviser among other designations Monday. He also nominated an economist and former securities regulator to lead the central bank in the aftermath of a major banking scandal that took down the nation’s president and led to the resignation of the monetary authority’s previous leader.Alliana submitted the nomination of Jorge Schreiner, who served on the central bank’s board of directors from 1997 to 1999, to lawmakers Monday, he said in a social media post. Schreiner also led Paraguay’s securities regulator from 2003 to 2013. Schreiner is set to replace Carlos Carvallo, the former chairman who resigned last week after the central bank intervened in Ueno Bank SA, a major consumer bank that collapsed due to insufficient liquidity. His nomination requires Senate confirmation.The failure left millions without access to accounts and plunged Paraguay into political turmoil. Former President Santiago Peña, who had business ties to Ueno’s controlling shareholder, was impeached Friday and is currently in pretrial detention after prosecutors charged him with breach of trust and self-enrichment over his alleged role in the bank’s collapse.Prosecutors and police over the weekend raided a luxurious mansion owned by Peña overlooking Lake Ypacarai, where authorities said they discovered a safe room underneath a swimming pool.Carvallo was charged with breach of trust, falsifying documents and self-enrichment. The central bank has been operating with just three of its five board members following his resignation and that of another board member last week.Schreiner’s “experience and track record in the financial system will be essential to strengthening the central bank’s institutional framework and restoring Paraguayans’ trust,” Alliana, who was sworn in as the nation’s new leader on Friday, said in the social media post.Alliana also said he’d nominated Fernando Rivarola, an economist and former central bank staffer, to fill the other vacant role on its board. As the monetary authority’s director of bank supervision, Rivarola gained prominence earlier this year after the leak of an internal memo he’d authored about alleged irregularities at Ueno. He left the position in July after being named to the board of state development bank AFD.Ueno had amassed more than 2.9 million clients in a country of roughly 6.1 million people, holding deposits for 17 trillion guaraníes ($2.8 billion), including about $355 million owed to social security agency IPS. The central bank said last week that Ueno clients have started to receive payments from the deposit insurance fund.(Updates to add cabinet changes in first, second paragraphs)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Stone-pelting fair 'Pathron Ka Mela' at Dhami in Himachal concluded in 18 minutes this year
content: Shimla: "Pathron Ka Mela" (stone-pelting fair), the centuries-old tradition, celebrated near Shimla, concluded in 18 minutes this year on Monday. .The mela, marked by the pelting of stones mainly by the youth of one group on another at Dhami in Himachal Pradesh's Shimla district, is held a day after the Diwali festival and continues until a person hit by a stone starts bleeding. Villagers smear "tilak" of blood on the forehead of the local goddess Maha Kali, marking the conclusion of the mela. .Supreme Court settles decade-old energy dispute, Himachal to get 11,973 MU electricity from Punjab, Haryana .The locals consider getting injured as auspicious and a blessing from the Goddess Maha Kali as the blood is smeared on her forehead. .This year, the stone-pelting continued for about 18 minutes until Mahesh Verma of the Jamog group sustained an injury and the mela came to an end after villagers smeared "tilak" of his blood on the forehead of the local goddess Maha Kali. .According to the legend, residents of Halog and Jamog villages line up on either side of the circular structure and shower small stones at each other. The fair begins after the priest of the Narsingh Devta temple reaches the Kali Devi temple, accompanied by musicians playing traditional instruments. .The tradition is very old but its exact year is not available, said Jagdeep Singh, a member of the erstwhile royal family. .The practice is more than three centuries old and the festival starts with members of the erstwhile royal family pelting the first stone after performing puja. As a precautionary measure, the game is played from a reasonably safe distance. .Locals say the festival started as an alternative to "sati". While the tradition of "sati" (in which a woman set herself ablaze after her husband's death) was in vogue, a king died and his queen ended her life following the cruel tradition. The people became deeply upset and started the mela, they say. .Youth from both sides are seen throwing stones with full strength. The mela lasted over half-an-hour last year and only 15 minutes in 2024. .Delhi protests | Ground report from Himachal Bhawan and Parliament Street.ICMR to establish high-altitude health research centre in Himachal Pradesh.Hundreds of people, including those from adjoining villages and also from Shimla and other places, assembled in large numbers at the Sports Ground to witness the stone-pelting competition and enjoy the warmth of the sun under a clear sky. Dhami is 30 km away from Shimla. .The local administration and human rights activists have been discouraging villagers from participating in the ritual by highlighting its cruelty. However, as the mela is deeply rooted in traditions, the locals are not ready to give it up and celebrate it every year in a grand manner without any reservations.

headline: 24.25 lakh housing blocks mapped across India using special software for Census
content: New Delhi: The Registrar General of India has mapped 24.25 lakh Houselisting Blocks, micro-units of up to 800 individuals that form the foundation of the country's population headcount, using a special software developed for the purpose, an official communique said. .The RGI used an ancillary application of the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS), a bespoke software backbone, designed to monitor the Census exercise in near real time, to map these blocks across the country. .Each House-Listing Block (HLB) of the House-listing and Housing Census will normally be taken as an Enumeration Block (EB) for Population Enumeration in the Census, a two-phased process -- the first stage is known as house listing and housing census, and the second stage is population enumeration. .The Houselisting Operation (HLO), constituting the first phase of Census 2027, was successfully completed across the States and Union Territories, except Manipur. ."During this phase, extensive digital mapping activities were also carried out through the Houselisting Block Creator (HLBC) Web Mapping Application, an ancillary application of the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS)...The application facilitated the digital demarcation of approximately 24.25 lakh Houselisting Blocks (HLBs) across the country, thereby creating a comprehensive geospatial framework for Census 2027," Registrar General of India and Census Commissioner Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan said in a latest communique. .GBA begins four-day training session for second phase of Census 2027.For the second phase of the Census, in which the population headcount will begin soon in areas other than Ladakh and in snow-bound, non-synchronous areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand and Manipur, the HLBs will form the basis for creating Enumeration Blocks for population enumeration. .In his latest letter to all states and union territories, Narayan said that, building on the successful completion of the HLO phase, certain mapping activities are required before the Population Enumeration (PE) phase begins. ."These include correction of Administrative Unit boundaries, if any, resolution of overlapping HLBs, coverage of Uncovered Habitation Areas, if any, splitting HLBs with more than manageable workload of an Enumerator by generation of Sub-Enumeration Blocks (Sub-EBs) and Supervisory Circle Maps," the letter said. .Narayan said timely completion of these activities is extremely essential for ensuring complete geographic coverage without any omission or duplication of the habitation areas in the Enumeration Blocks and also operational preparedness for Population Enumeration. .The decennial exercise, scheduled for 2021, was postponed due to the COVID-19 outbreak. The Union Cabinet has approved Rs 11,718 crore for conducting the Census, which will be the biggest headcount exercise. .Population enumeration in Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and areas other than snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand will take place from December 1, 2026, to January 4, 2027, because of the assembly elections. The Central Government has deferred the house-listing operations for Census 2027 for Manipur, a notification issued by RGI said last month. .The exercise in Ladakh and snow-bound non-synchronous areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand took place from September 1 to 30. .In the rest of the country, the population census shall be undertaken from January 25, 2027, to February 28, 2027.

headline: DA hike news: Uttar Pradesh govt increases dearness allowance by 3% for employees — Check who is eligible
content: DA hike news: Uttar Pradesh has increased dearness allowance by 3%, from 60% of basic pay to 63%, with effect from 1 July 2026, the state government said in an order issued on Saturday. This decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the state and provide financial relief amid Diwali festivities, PTI reported. UP DA hike: Who is eligible? The hike will be implemented for Uttar Pradesh state government employees, staff in aided educational and technical institutions, regular and full-time employees of urban local bodies, work-charged employees, and those serving on University Grants Commission (UGC) pay scales, the report said. How will arrears be paid? The increased DA for October will be paid along with regular salary for November 2026, according to the PTI report.Further, an ANI report added that arrears for the preceding four months period between July to September 2026, will be deposited separately into employees' provident fund (PF) accounts. UP Sub-Inspectors, Platoon Commanders appointed Earlier, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath gave appointment letters to 4,543 newly selected Sub-Inspectors and Platoon Commanders in Lucknow, the ANI report added. “Under the ‘Mission Rozgar’, appointment letters were handed over today in Lucknow to 4,543 newly selected Sub-Inspectors and Platoon Commanders in UP Police through a fair and transparent recruitment process,” the chief minister wrote on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter). DA hike announcements ahead of Diwali 2026 DA is a percentage of employees' basic pay that aims to mitigate the impact of the rising cost of living and inflation. As per the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) recommendations, the Centre revises DA twice annually, using data from the All-India Consumer Price Index (AICPI). These announcements usually come in March and October, with rollouts in January and July. Effective from 1 July, the Centre's “Diwali gift” is the second DA increase this year, after it hiked the component by 2% in April from 58% to 60%, effective from 1 January for more than 1 crore beneficiaries — approximately 48.54 lakh central government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners across the country. Notably, besides the Finance Ministry's announcement on 28 October, state governments also hiked DA for employees and pensioners ahead of Diwali. This includes a 5% hike by the Himachal Pradesh government, 3% DA hikes each by the Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Punjab, Arunachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Gujarat governments, 2.5% increase by the Karnataka government, and 2% increases by the Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Kerala governments. (With inputs from Agencies)

headline: HRTC to Operate 266 Special Buses for Diwali
content: The corporation will operate 134 buses on November 6 and 132 on November 7. On November 6, the schedule includes 42 buses from Delhi, 69 from Chandigarh and 23 from Baddi, with services planned for different destinations in Himachal Pradesh. On November 7, 49 buses will depart from Delhi, 63 from Chandigarh and 20 from Baddi. The corporation has begun preparations to support convenient travel and provide additional transport capacity during the festive period. Agnihotri said the special arrangements had been planned because people generally wanted to celebrate Diwali with their families. The services will benefit passengers travelling from Delhi, Chandigarh, Baddi and other locations to their home districts in the state. The HRTC will also maintain minimum bus services on Diwali day. Buses will remain available on important routes, including connections to Delhi, Chandigarh and other long-distance destinations, according to requirements. Within Himachal Pradesh, bus services will operate until 4 pm on November 8. headline: Baddi air quality worst in Himachal
content: Shimla: Air quality in the industrial town of Baddi in Solan district was the worst across Himachal Pradesh on Diwali day, with an AQI of 376.According to the Himachal Pradesh Pollution Control Board, Baddi recorded an AQI of 369 on Nov 7, which climbed to 376 on Nov 8 and dropped to 344 on Monday at 5 pm.The AQI level between 301 and 400 is categorised as very poor.Meanwhile, multiple forest fires were reported in Kullu district on Diwali night, with sparks from firecrackers suspected to have triggered some of the blazes.A fire broke out in the forest behind Sultanpur, near the district headquarters, Kullu, on Diwali night, triggering panic among residents. Locals joined hands to douse the flames and managed to bring the fire under control.Fires also continued to smoulder through the night in the Pij, Khokhan and Diyar areas adjoining the Bhekli forest near Kullu town, with flames visible from a distance.Forest fires were also reported from different parts of the Maharaja Valley in Kullu on Monday morning. Around 1 pm, a fire broke out near the Baba Balak Nath temple at Tikra Bawdi along the Kullu-Bhuntar road.According to an officer, a fire brigade team rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control after considerable effort.Another fire was reported from the forest area of Dobhi village near Patlikuhal.Forest department officials said they were taking steps to extinguish the fires.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news.
